newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges N.Korea not to test missile.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges N.Korea not to test missile.

text.p: The United States said Friday it had sent a "very strong message" to North Korea not to carry out a medium-range ballistic missile test that Pyongyang was reported to have been preparing.
A U.S. military spokesman in Tokyo said Wednesday that the United States had sent an advanced reconnaissance plane to monitor a possible test firing into the sea near Japan.
In Washington, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said: "We have conveyed a very strong message to the North Koreans that they ought not to undertake such a test."

"Should North Korea undertake such a missile test, it would be destabilising, it would be harmful to our efforts to provide stability in the Korean Peninsula, and the United States would very much be opposed to this," he told reporters.
Burns said Washington had made this clear in what he called very recent contacts with the North Koreans.

The spokesman declined to spell out where and when the contacts took place. He noted that the United States habitually spoke to the North Koreans through Pyongyang's mission to the United Nations, but also had "other ways of passing messages".

"This is a very serious issue. We think it would be destabilising in North Asia to have these types of tests undertaken. And North Korea needs to think very carefully about this kind of action," Burns said.
He said he was unable to comment on the status of the possible North Korean test.
Japanese defence officials said this week that North Korea had made all the preparations for a test firing, including stationing ships in the area where a missile would land.

But they did not rule out that the activity could be part of an elaborate game of nerves to back up verbal threats to make South Korea and its allies pay for the capture of a North Korean submarine which Seoul says infiltrated its territory.
According to the officials, the missile involved is the Rodong-1, which is based on the Soviet Scud design. With a 600-mile (1,000-km) range, it could easily hit many parts of Japan including Tokyo.
